dossier.purpose: Curated collection of 161 Claude Code subagent definitions. Each is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (name, description, tools, and usually model) in 10 category folders under categories/. It is distributed as 10 Claude Code plugins through a marketplace manifest, and also by manual copy or installer scripts. It is a subagent collection (CLAUDE.md:7), not a SKILL.md skills collection: no SKILL.md, AGENTS.md or Codex-format file exists in the repo. The security and engineering content is mostly keyword-bullet checklists (e.g. categories/04-quality-security/security-auditor.md, penetration-tester.md, code-reviewer.md; categories/03-infrastructure/security-engineer.md), plus a few shorter rewritten agents (ad-security-reviewer.md, auth-integration-engineer.md).

claims.claim: "The awesome collection of 161+ Claude Code subagents across 10 categories" (badge also says 161).
The repo is "the definitive collection of Claude Code subagents, specialized AI assistants designed for specific development tasks."
Contributions must stay "vendor-neutral in their content"; PRs whose primary purpose is to promote a product are not accepted; sponsorship is the supported way to surface a product.

Recommended install is as a Claude Code plugin: `claude plugin marketplace add VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents` then `claude plugin install <plugin-name>`; one plugin per category (e.g. voltagent-qa-sec for Quality & Security). voltagent-meta works best with other categories installed.
Manual install: clone, then copy desired agent files to ~/.claude/agents/ (global) or .claude/agents/ (project).

Interactive installer lets you "browse categories, select agents, and install/uninstall them"; standalone variant "Downloads agents directly from GitHub without cloning the repository. Requires curl."
An agent-installer subagent can be curl-installed to ~/.claude/agents/ and used from Claude Code to find and install other agents.
Every subagent "operates within its own isolated context space" and has "Granular Tool Permissions"; isolated contexts give "Memory Efficiency".
"Claude Code will automatically engage it when suitable, or you can explicitly request its help."

"Smart Model Routing": each subagent includes a `model` field; opus for security-auditor, architect-reviewer, fintech-engineer; sonnet for python-pro, backend-developer, devops-engineer; haiku for documentation-engineer, seo-specialist, build-engineer.
Tool assignment: read-only agents (reviewers, auditors) get `Read, Grep, Glob`; "Each agent has minimal necessary permissions."
subagent-catalog is a "Claude Code skill" with /subagent-catalog:search, :fetch, :list, :invalidate; install with `cp -r tools/subagent-catalog ~/.claude/commands/`.
MIT licence; subagents are "as is"; "We do not audit or guarantee the security or correctness of any subagent. Review before use."

Codex is mentioned only in sponsor copy ("reach developers using AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and more") and in link-reference definitions pointing to a separate repo, VoltAgent/awesome-codex-subagents.

install.command:
claude plugin marketplace add VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents
claude plugin install <plugin-name>   # e.g. voltagent-lang, voltagent-infra, voltagent-qa-sec
No command given. Clone the repo, then copy the desired agent .md files to ~/.claude/agents/ (global) or .claude/agents/ (project).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry or analytics code in install-agents.sh, tools/subagent-catalog/config.sh or the workflow (searched for telemetry|analytics|tracking|beacon; only unrelated README text matched). No account or API key is required. Network use happens on user action only. install-agents.sh remote mode calls https://api.github.com/repos/VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents/contents and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents/main, unauthenticated (install-agents.sh:27-28, 55, 85, 110). subagent-catalog fetches README.md from raw.githubusercontent.com (config.sh:10, 40; 5 s connect / 30 s max) and caches it 12 h at ~/.claude/cache/subagent-catalog.md (config.sh:8-9). agent-installer.md:22-24 uses the same endpoints and notes the 60 req/h unauthenticated limit (:72). `claude plugin marketplace add VoltAgent/...` needs GitHub access (README.md:78). The README embeds remote images and a UTM-tagged sponsor link (README.md:2, 16-19, 38, 517), which are contacted only when the README is rendered or clicked. Individual agents add third-party network dependencies: BGPT remote MCP https://bgpt.pro/mcp/sse (scientific-literature-researcher.md:32), `npm install -g unslop` (content-quality-editor.md:18), `npm install -g prompt-to-asset` (visual-asset-generator.md:31), and `curl -fsSL .../ajhcs/healthcare-agents/main/install.sh | bash` (healthcare-admin.md:197).

languages: Markdown (161 agent files, 10 category READMEs, 4 slash-command files)

entry_points.what: Interactive bash installer/uninstaller for agent files. Local-copy or remote (GitHub API + raw) mode; installs to ~/.claude/agents or .claude/agents; no CLI flags; main at :571-583.
Claude Code marketplace manifest 'voltagent-subagents' listing 10 category plugins by relative source path (:11-92).
Ten per-category plugin manifests: name, version, metadata and an explicit `agents` array of ./*.md. No hooks, mcpServers, commands or skills keys in any JSON file.
161 subagent definitions: YAML frontmatter (name, description, tools, model on 153 of them) plus prompt body. This is the unit Claude Code loads.
Subagent (tools: Bash, WebFetch, Read, Write, Glob; model: haiku) that lists, installs and uninstalls agents via GitHub API/raw URLs.
Slash-command Markdown plus shared bash config. Fetches README.md from raw.githubusercontent.com and caches it 12 h at ~/.claude/cache/subagent-catalog.md.
The only CI workflow: PR check that category plugin versions are bumped and match marketplace.json.

code.architecture: Content-only repository with no build step or runtime service. categories/01..10-*/ each hold agent Markdown files (frontmatter + prompt), a category README.md and .claude-plugin/plugin.json with an explicit agents array. .claude-plugin/marketplace.json aggregates the ten category plugins. Distribution paths: (1) Claude Code plugin marketplace, (2) manual copy into ~/.claude/agents or .claude/agents, (3) install-agents.sh (bash menu; local cp at :543 or remote curl at :104-115), (4) agent-installer.md, (5) tools/subagent-catalog slash commands. Agents reference each other only by name in prose ('Integration with other agents'); no code links them. 115 of 161 agent files tell the agent to 'Query context manager', and 130 have a '## Communication Protocol' JSON section; no code in the repo implements that exchange. Size: about 37.6k lines across the 161 agent files, typically 277-287 lines for the templated ones (e.g. security-auditor.md is 287 lines) and 52-98 lines for newer ones (ad-security-reviewer.md 56, gdpr-ccpa-compliance.md 98). The 17-agent quality-security category is about 3.9k lines. All 161 agents have `description:` and `tools:`; 153 have `model:` (haiku 19, sonnet 109, inherit 25, opus 0). CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md define the contributor format.
code.packaging_and_release: No build artifacts, release workflow, checksums, signatures or attestations. No tags are visible in this shallow checkout (.git/packed-refs lists only origin/main). Distribution is by git: the Claude Code marketplace points at ./categories/* sources in this repo (marketplace.json:11-92). Versions are hand-maintained per category plugin (1.0.1 to 1.1.1 across plugin.json files) while marketplace.json metadata.version is 1.0.4 (marketplace.json:8). CONTRIBUTING.md:46-56 requires a version bump whenever a category .md changes, and CI enforces it (.github/workflows/enforce-plugin-version-bump.yml:38-77). The installers and catalog tool download from the mutable `main` branch with no pinning or integrity check (install-agents.sh:28, 104-115; config.sh:10, 40).
code.tests_and_ci: No test framework, test directories or test files: searched for test/tests/spec dirs and *.bats, *.test.*, *.spec.*, approximately 0 test files. One CI workflow, .github/workflows/enforce-plugin-version-bump.yml, on ubuntu-latest with actions/checkout@v4 (tag-pinned, not SHA-pinned). It triggers on pull_request touching categories/** or .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, and on workflow_dispatch (:3-8). It (1) fails if any .md under a category changed versus the base but that category's plugin.json version did not (:38-52), and (2) fails if a category plugin.json version differs from its marketplace.json entry (:54-77). It does not lint frontmatter, links, agent counts, plugin `agents` arrays or the shell scripts.
code.dependencies: No dependency manifests (no package.json, pyproject/requirements, Cargo.toml, go.mod, Gemfile or lockfiles), so 0 declared direct dependencies. The shell scripts use bash, curl, awk, sed, grep, date (install-agents.sh; tools/subagent-catalog/config.sh). Some agent bodies tell users to install external tools (unslop and prompt-to-asset npm packages, a BGPT remote MCP, a healthcare-agents install script); none of these is declared as a dependency.
code.security_policy: none. No SECURITY.md exists in the repo or .github/ (the only file there is workflows/enforce-plugin-version-bump.yml). README.md:524-526 gives an 'as is', no-audit disclaimer and says to open an issue for problems or removal requests.

risks: Scope: this is a subagent collection, not a SKILL.md skills collection. No SKILL.md, AGENTS.md or Codex-format file exists, and Codex appears only in sponsor text and unused link references (README.md:129, 529-530; the separate awesome-codex-subagents repo was not read). On its own it offers no Codex loading path and no per-task skill loader.

Activation granularity and size: the Claude Code install unit is a whole category plugin (10 plugins of 11-30 agents; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json:11-92). Narrower installs need manual copying or the installer scripts (README.md:92-120). Agent files are long: about 37.6k lines across 161 files, typically 277-287 lines each (e.g. categories/04-quality-security/security-auditor.md is 287 lines, and the 17-agent qa-sec category is about 3.9k lines), so concise canonical rules are not what most files provide.

Uneven content form: older templated agents are keyword-bullet checklists with a pseudo 'Communication Protocol' JSON and invented sample metrics (security-auditor.md:127-142, 196-208, 224-225; penetration-tester.md:127-142, 196-208, 224-225). 115 of 161 files say 'Query context manager', though no code implements that exchange and context-manager.md:12 says it only works with files. Only 12 files contain explicit no-fabrication language (mostly category 09, e.g. context-manager.md:10-15). Numbers inside agent files are illustrative, not measurements.

Broad tool grants: 118 of 161 agents list Bash and 142 list Write or Edit; only security-auditor.md:4 and compliance-auditor.md:4 are exactly Read, Grep, Glob (contrast README.md:482, 487). penetration-tester.md:4 has Bash and lists exploit development, evasion, persistence and 'cover track analysis' topics (:47-55, :97-105). Its authorization gating is prompt text only (:17-18, :148-170, :267-275). ui-ux-tester.md:4 declares chrome-mcp and computer-use. README.md:524 disclaims any security audit.

Unpinned, unverified supply chain: installers and the catalog download from the mutable `main` branch with no checksum or signature (install-agents.sh:27-28, 104-115; tools/subagent-catalog/config.sh:10, 40; README.md:110, 118). Agent bodies instruct third-party installs: `npm install -g unslop` (content-quality-editor.md:18), `npm install -g prompt-to-asset` (visual-asset-generator.md:31), `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajhcs/healthcare-agents/main/install.sh | bash` (healthcare-admin.md:197), and a hosted MCP at https://bgpt.pro/mcp/sse (scientific-literature-researcher.md:32).

Metadata drift and no tests: README says 161 (README.md:9) but marketplace.json:9 says 158, and the manifests list 160 (voltagent-dev-exp omits docs-drift-editor: categories/06-developer-experience/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:11-27). The README model table contradicts frontmatter (README.md:473 vs security-auditor.md:5; 0 agents use opus; 8 lack `model:`). agent-installer.md:52-54 shows stale counts (11/22/14 vs actual 13/30/16). There are no tests; CI only checks version bumps (enforce-plugin-version-bump.yml:38-77). No evals or measurements of the collection itself are published; the only figures concern other projects (README.md:353; healthcare-admin.md:194).

Governance and maintenance: no SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS, changelog, release process or artifacts, and no tags visible in the checkout. Versions are bumped by hand (CONTRIBUTING.md:46-56). Contributions are community-sourced and unaudited (README.md:524), and the README carries sponsor and promotional blocks (README.md:34-71) next to a vendor-neutral policy (README.md:32). .claude/settings.local.json is present in the checkout despite .gitignore:16 listing .claude/, and pre-approves Bash(python3:*), Bash(for:*) and Bash(git status:*) for anyone opening a clone in Claude Code (.claude/settings.local.json:4-8).

Licensing and attribution: LICENSE is MIT with only 'Copyright (c) 2025 VoltAgent' (LICENSE:3), while the README says the repo aggregates maintainer and community contributions (README.md:524). At least one agent is adapted from third-party work (ai-writing-auditor.md:65-70 credits conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing as MIT, plus brandonwise/humanizer). No NOTICE or third-party license text file exists in the repo, only the in-file credit.
